posts.body:
The National Examinations Council (NECO) has released the results of the 2026 Senior School Certificate Examination (SSCE).

A total of 1,378,048 candidates registered for the examination, comprising 682,352 males and 695,696 females.Of the registered candidates, 1,371,992 sat for the examination, including 678,903 males and 693,089 females.
NECO said 804,948 candidates, representing 58.67 per cent, obtained at least five credits including English Language and Mathematics.
The council also disclosed that 1,162,118 candidates, representing 84.70 per cent, obtained five credits and above irrespective of their performance in English Language and Mathematics.
posts.title: NECO Releases 2026 SSCE Results, 58.67% Secure Five Credits Including English, Maths

posts.body:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s extended stay abroad has continued to generate debate around constitutional provisions that require the president to transmit power to the vice president if away from the country for more than 21 days or unable to discharge the functions of his office.The president, who was supposed to return to Nigeria on September 20, had extended his “working vacation” by a week and the presidency said he would be back in the country over the weekend. But he did not return as promised, raising fresh concerns over the handling of his whereabouts.The Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD) had urged Nigerians to seek judicial interpretation of President Tinubu’s prolonged absence from the country, saying citizens have the right to challenge actions they believe violate the Constitution.

The Director of CDD-West Africa, Dr Dauda Garuba, said although the president had the right to travel and extend his stay, he was expected to take the provisions of the Constitution into consideration when determining the duration of his absence.

President Tinubu Reportedly Asks Court To Stop FBI, DEA From Releasing Records Linked To Her%in Tr@fficking Allegations



The case also concerns records allegedly connected to a 1993 civil forfeiture proceeding involving about $460,000 linked to Tinubu. Tinubu has denied wrongdoing.

In a 16-page court document filed by his legal team and shared with Channels Television Saturday, Tinubu argued that releasing the records could violate his privacy.

His lawyers said information disclosed during the forfeiture proceeding did not reveal details or outcome of any possible criminal investigation. They said Greenspan sought the records because the information is unavailable, and public disclosure of some details does not eliminate Tinubu’s privacy interest in undisclosed portions.

They cited the Supreme Court’s Reporters Committee precedent, saying individuals can retain privacy interests in government records even when portions were public.
They also referenced a 2012 Judicial Watch decision involving the DOJ, arguing that people can retain privacy interests in investigative information even when publicly linked to criminal activity.
Another case involving the Electronic Privacy Information Center and the DOJ was cited to argue that being investigated is separate from the investigation’s contents.

“Regardless of the prior disclosure in the forfeiture proceeding, Intervenor retains a privacy interest in potential disclosure of the investigative files sought by Plaintiff,” the document stated.

The dispute centres on whether the US government should release the investigative records, with Tinubu seeking to prevent disclosure on privacy grounds.
posts.title: President Bola Tinubu has asked a US court to stop DOJ, FBI and DEA from releasing his her%in related records
posts.excerpt:
President Bola Tinubu has asked a US court to stop DOJ, FBI and DEA from releasing records on past investigations.
The development follows a FOIA lawsuit by transparency activist Aaron Greenspan, seeking Tinubu investigation documents. His requests include the FBI file on Tinubu and Form 302 interview records from 1992 to 1993.

posts.excerpt: Former Liverpool footballer Mohamed Salah has been banned from driving for six months after his Rolls-Royce was clocked speeding.
posts.body:
Salah failed to tell police who was at the wheel when the car was caught by a speed camera driving at 36mph (58 km/h) on a 30mph (48km/h) stretch of road in Wilmslow, Cheshire, on 27 March, according to court documents.

The 34-year-old did not respond to the notice of the prosecution, brought by Cheshire Police, and did not enter a plea to the charge.

He was handed a six-month driving ban and ordered to pay £1,044 in a hearing at Warrington Combined Court.

A court spokeswoman said Salah was prosecuted under the Single Justice Procedure, which sees magistrates sit in private hearings, and was convicted of failing to give information relating to the identification of the driver of the Rolls-Royce.
posts.title: MOHAMMED SALAH FACES DRIVING BAN

posts.author: FSTV Desk
posts.body:
Nollywood actor, director and producer Ugezu J Ugezu has criticized what he described as unfavorable payment and exclusivity terms offered to filmmakers by Africa Magic. 
“What they offer most of the times is nothing to write home about,” Ugezu said. “If you film for like ₦5 million and they watch the movie, the highest they can say they pay you ₦1.5 million.”
Speaking on GBAM, Ugezu claimed that producers could spend about ₦5 million making a film, only for the platform to offer around ₦1.5 million for it while requiring that the movie not be shown elsewhere.

posts.title: FOOTBALL LEGEND LIONEL ANDRÉS MESSI DROPS BOMBSHELL ON RETIREMENT
posts.body:
After 20 years, Lionel Messi has retired from the Argentina national team.

The 39-year-old announced it on Instagram today. "It hurts to my core, but it's the right time," he wrote. "I gave everything for this jersey."
He drafted the message after the 2026 World Cup final loss to Spain, and decided to post it after his dad Jorge passed away.

Messi leaves as Argentina’s top scorer: 125 goals in 207 games. World Cup 2022 winner + 2x Copa America champion.
He’s NOT retiring from football, he’ll keep playing for Inter Miami. 
"Now I’ll cheer from the sidelines. Thank you. ¡Vamos Argentina!"
An era ends 💔

posts.title: OPAY DEBUNKS INDEFINITE SHUTDOWN RUMOR CIRCULATING IN THE MEDIA SPACE
posts.excerpt: Leading  fintech company, OPay Digital Services, has dismissed as false and malicious a viral social media publication claiming that the company would embark on a prolonged break from September 1, 2026, urging its customers to withdraw or move their funds.
posts.body:
Leading  fintech company, OPay Digital Services, has dismissed as false and malicious a viral social media publication claiming that the company would embark on a prolonged break from September 1, 2026, urging its customers to withdraw or move their funds. 
The fabricated publication, which gained traction across social media platforms on Sunday, purportedly warned OPay customers that the fintech would shut down its operations for an extended period beginning September 1.

However, OPay, in an official response published across its verified social media platforms, described the claim as false, assuring customers that the company remains fully operational.

In a statement titled, ‘This is FALSE,’ the fintech said: “OPay is not going on break by September. We’re here, and we’re going nowhere!”

posts.title: BRADLEY BARCOLA SIGNS A 5 YEAR CONTRACT WITH LIVERPOOL FC
posts.body:
Liverpool have completed the signing of France forward Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain in a deal worth up to £123 million, strengthening their squad ahead of the new Premier League season.

The transfer was confirmed by BBC Sport, with Liverpool paying an initial £106 million plus £17 million in potential add-ons for the 23-year-old.
Barcola has signed a five-year contract and becomes Liverpool’s fifth new arrival of the summer, following Victor Munoz, Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo and Ifeanyi Ndukwe.

He pledged to pay the “new bride price” of any woman who left her marriage over allegiance to the party.The comment has sparked outrage across the state, with many residents, including Islamic scholars, describing it as reckless, provocative and capable of undermining family values.

American rapper Cardi B has seemingly hinted that fans could see more of Nigerian footballer Maduka Okoye as dating rumours surrounding the pair continue to grow.
The rapper, who is currently featured on the cover of Vogue Arabia, opened up about her music, motherhood and love life following her divorce, with her recent outings with Okoye also coming up during the interview.
Cardi and the 27-year-old Udinese goalkeeper first sparked romance speculation after they were spotted together at Paris Fashion Week in July. The footballer was seen helping Cardi get settled into her seat before sitting beside her as they watched the fashion show.

Speaking about Okoye, Cardi described him as “really sweet” and “very kind,” noting that although he appears “very strict” and “stern” on social media, he is different in person.
When asked if fans should expect to see more of the Nigerian footballer, Cardi responded with a giggle, “I hope so.”

Neither Cardi nor Okoye has publicly confirmed the nature of their relationship, but the rapper’s latest comments have only added to speculation that something could be developing between them.

posts.title: Veteran actor Olu Jacobs dies at 84
posts.body:
Veteran Nigerian actor and film executive, Oludotun Baiyewu Jacobs, popularly known as Olu Jacobs, has died at the age of 84.

His death was announced by his son, Olusoji Jacobs, on Instagram on Wednesday.

In the statement, the family described the late actor as “The Lion of Lufodo” and asked bloggers and social media influencers to respect its privacy.

“It is with gratitude to God for a life well lived and fought, that we announce the passing of our dear husband, father, grandfather and uncle. The Lion of Lufodo.

“Whoever shows us a finger, we are ready to cut off his fingers,” Buba stated, adding, “We are now playing politics. Whoever shows us a finger, we will show him a finger… Whoever dares to show us a finger again, we will break his finger.”

“The government is our government. Those who follow us will enjoy the honey; if you refuse, then you will be flogged,” he said.
